text:
chief complaint: headache for about one week, described as a dull pain in the back of the head.
history of present illness: headache began about a week ago, likely in the setting of stress, and comes and goes with relief from acetaminophen or ibuprofen that wears off; worse in the evening; no neck or shoulder discomfort reported; no fever, no visual changes, no head trauma; not the worst headache of the patient's life; patient has had similar headaches previously; blood glucose not monitored; poor diet and no exercise over the past week due to headache and stress.
physical examination: normal except for mild paraspinal tenderness and muscle tightness in the cervical spine and bilateral trapezius; no papilledema; extraocular motions intact; grade 3/6 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior exam.
symptoms experienced by the patient: dull occipital headache, facial flushing with warmth in the ears, mild dizziness with headaches.
new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: flexeril 5 mg three times a day; metformin 500 mg twice daily continued (no change).
follow-up instructions: return in four weeks; check blood sugars daily and bring readings; labs ordered (hemoglobin A1c, CBC, CHEM-12); return sooner or call if headache worsens, becomes sudden or severe, develops fever, or does not improve within a few days on Flexeril; resume exercise.
